patterns.name: Renamed API Parameters
patterns.description: AI renames request parameters in the route handler schema but callers in other files still send the old parameter names, causing validation failures at runtime.

testPattern.description: Verify caller does not send old parameter names

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/Writewyze/qodo-test-shared-models/pull/1 — Cursor renamed email → emailAddress in schema and most validators but missed the length-check reader on line 29; Cursor Bugbot caught it in its own PR review; also https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/35852 — dispatch built args['path'] but both _handle_rename implementations read args['old_path'] causing KeyError on every rename

patterns.name: Changed Response Shape
patterns.description: AI restructures the API response object (e.g., wraps data in a nested key) but callers destructure the old shape, causing TypeError at runtime when accessing missing properties.

testPattern.description: Verify caller handles new response shape

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/Monichre/digital-mischief-group/pull/1 — Firecrawl v2 API changed branding fields into a nested data envelope; callers destructuring top-level payload.branding broke silently; fix added fallback for both shapes

patterns.name: New Required Field Not Sent by Callers
patterns.description: AI adds a new required field to the API schema but callers in the blast radius do not send this field, causing schema validation errors (e.g., Zod parse failure) on every call.

testPattern.description: Verify caller sends newly required field

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/cyruzin/golang-tmdb/issues/95 — struct missing required API fields (adult, known_for_department, original_name, popularity) after schema update

patterns.name: Removed Field Still Sent by Callers
patterns.description: AI removes a field from the API schema (strict validation mode) but callers still send it, causing validation failures or silent data loss depending on schema strictness.

testPattern.description: Verify caller no longer sends removed field

patterns.name: HTTP Status Code Changed
patterns.description: AI changes the HTTP status code returned by an endpoint (e.g., 201→200) but callers check the old status code to determine success, causing silent logic failures.

testPattern.description: Verify caller handles updated status code

patterns.name: Idempotency Key Not Sent by Callers
patterns.description: AI adds an idempotency key requirement to a payment or mutation endpoint schema but callers that trigger the endpoint do not generate or send the idempotency key, causing duplicate operations.

testPattern.description: Verify caller sends idempotency key

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/adamrodi/groundwork/pull/6 — Stripe PaymentIntent created without idempotency key; code review identified the gap and fix added idempotency key to PaymentIntent creation call

patterns.name: Auth Check Without Ownership Verification
patterns.description: AI adds authentication check (user is logged in) to a new endpoint but omits ownership check (user owns the resource), enabling any authenticated user to access any other user's data (IDOR vulnerability).

testPattern.description: Verify ownership check is performed after auth check

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/fagemx/edda/issues/288 — router() exposed publicly without auth middleware; post_scope_check accepted arbitrary project_id without verifying caller owned the resource; fix scoped router to pub(crate) and added ownership validation

patterns.name: New Endpoint Added Outside Auth Middleware
patterns.description: AI adds a new route or endpoint file outside the authenticated router group, bypassing all authentication middleware. The endpoint is publicly accessible when it should be protected.

testPattern.description: Verify auth middleware is applied to new endpoint

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/OneStepAt4time/aegis/issues/349 — new route hooks added outside authenticated router group using broad startsWith('/v1/hooks') match, making unintended paths publicly accessible; fix switched to exact path matching with auth on all endpoints

patterns.name: Sanitization at HTTP Boundary Bypassed by Internal Callers
patterns.description: AI adds input sanitization at the HTTP handler level but internal callers (background jobs, service methods) call the underlying service function directly, bypassing sanitization entirely.

testPattern.description: Verify all callers pass through sanitization layer

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/am225723/quoagent/pull/33 — Jules built /api/run, /api/approve, /api/contacts/* with zero auth; Jules Sentinel then discovered the gap and wrote its own post-mortem: 'The /api/run endpoint was completely unprotected. The presence of a CRON_SECRET in the environment is useless if the code does not check it.'

patterns.name: Multi-Step Operation Without Database Transaction
patterns.description: AI implements a multi-step write operation (debit + credit, create + update) as sequential database calls without wrapping in a transaction. Partial failures leave the database in an inconsistent state.

testPattern.description: Verify atomic operation is wrapped in transaction

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/adssoccer1/finserv-monorepo/issues/11 — LedgerService.recordPayment() writes DEBIT and CREDIT sequentially with no transaction boundary; crash between writes leaves ledger permanently imbalanced; also https://github.com/ChainSafe/canton-middleware/issues/171 — EVM store SaveEvmTransaction, SaveEvmLog, NextEvmBlock executed as independent statements causing orphaned records on partial failure

patterns.name: Delete/Update Without Cascading to Related Entities
patterns.description: AI implements a delete or update operation on a parent entity but does not cascade the operation to related child entities, leaving orphaned records or inconsistent state.

testPattern.description: Verify cascade delete/update calls are made to related entities

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/jurjans/ksj-wp-func/commit/e735faf677f2f8060b7f100db4265a06444a94ce — Claude dead-code removal deleted get_model() from function_app.py (looked unused) but fb_gen.py called it internally; required two separate restore commits; also https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/35852 — both middleware classes (_StateClaudeFileToolMiddleware and _FilesystemClaudeFileToolMiddleware) were generated from the same flawed template with the wrong key name

patterns.name: Event Emission Dropped During Refactor
patterns.description: AI refactors an event-emitting handler and silently drops the event emission call. Downstream listeners and notification handlers never fire, breaking async workflows.

testPattern.description: Verify event is emitted after state change

patterns.name: Write Handler Loses Cache Invalidation
patterns.description: AI rewrites a write handler and loses the cache invalidation call. Subsequent reads return stale cached data until TTL expires, causing data consistency issues.

testPattern.description: Verify cache is invalidated after write

patterns.name: ORM Schema Updated Without Migration File
patterns.description: AI updates the ORM schema model (Prisma, SQLAlchemy, Drizzle) to add fields or change column types but does not create the corresponding migration file. The database schema lags behind the code.

testPattern.description: Verify migration file exists for schema change

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24433 — Prisma schema for LiteLLM_MCPServerTable updated with source_url column but migration file not generated; column missing on every container restart causing runtime errors; also https://github.com/sarathfranciswork/ignite/issues/270 — squashed migration files inconsistent with schema causing drift in production

patterns.name: Return Type Widened to Include Null
patterns.description: AI changes a function return type from T to T|null (or adds undefined) but callers access properties on the return value without null checks, causing runtime TypeError on the null path.

testPattern.description: Verify caller handles null return case

patterns.name: Error Handler Swallows Exceptions Silently
patterns.description: AI wraps a critical operation in a try/catch that swallows all errors without re-throwing or logging. Failures become invisible: callers' catch blocks never fire, monitoring sees no errors.

testPattern.description: Verify errors propagate to caller

patterns.name: Async forEach Fire-and-Forget
patterns.description: AI writes arr.forEach(async item => await fn(item)) not realising forEach ignores returned promises. Each async callback fires without being awaited — errors are silently swallowed and callers observe completion before work is done.

testPattern.description: Verify all async operations complete before caller proceeds

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/304898 — forEach(async ...) causing fire-and-forget promises in notebook code; fixed by switching to Promise.all
patterns.aiNativeReason: Human developers know forEach is synchronous; LLMs learn the async/await pattern without learning the iterator contract

patterns.name: Provider Config Updated in One File, Missed Elsewhere
patterns.description: AI updates an LLM provider, API key reference, or service config in the file it is editing but leaves stale references in other files. The app boots with split config — one path uses the new provider, another still calls the old one.

testPattern.description: Verify all config references resolve to the same provider/key

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/MalikAhmad911/infinite-rankers/pull/1 — Claude PR author renamed NEON_DATABASE_URL → DATABASE_URL in code; .env.example still had old key + wrong PORT; also https://github.com/theideaiq/monorepo/pull/660 — Jules bot created 4 separate PRs to fix Zod schema keys missing from .env.example
patterns.aiNativeReason: AI applies changes to the file in scope; it does not grep the codebase for all references the way a human doing a provider swap would

patterns.name: Nested Property Access Without Null Guard
patterns.description: AI accesses deeply nested properties (obj.user.profile.avatar) on values that can be null or undefined, without optional chaining or null guards. The happy path in training data rarely shows the null case so the guard is omitted.

testPattern.description: Verify accessor handles null/undefined at each chain level

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/open-feature/java-sdk-contrib/pull/1709 — null pointer exception from missing descriptor check on optional value; fix added null guard before access
patterns.aiNativeReason: LLMs are trained on happy-path examples; null/undefined branches appear less frequently in training data so guards are systematically omitted

patterns.name: Error Response Cast to Type Without Runtime Validation
patterns.description: AI uses TypeScript 'as' assertions to cast API error responses or exception objects to a typed shape without verifying the shape at runtime. When the actual error differs (e.g., string vs object), code accesses undefined fields silently.

testPattern.description: Verify error response shape is validated before field access

patterns.ossEvidence: https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/pull/39428 — Twilio SMS provider used catch (e: any) and accessed e.message directly; when a non-Error value was thrown, e.message was undefined causing agents to receive 'undefined' notification; fix replaced as-cast with instanceof narrowing
patterns.aiNativeReason: AI knows the intended type from context and asserts it confidently; it doesn't model the possibility that the runtime value diverges from the declared shape

patterns.name: Unit Test Mocks the Same Assumption the Code Has
patterns.description: AI writes a unit test that mocks a dependency to return the exact shape the code was written to expect. Both the code and the mock share the same incorrect assumption about the contract. The test passes. The real caller sends a different shape and gets a runtime error. Optinum generates a test against the real contract, not the mocked one.

testPattern.description: Verify real caller payload matches actual contract, not the mocked shape

patterns.ossEvidence: OSS-search: GitHub issues where unit tests pass but integration fails on a field that was mocked in test — search 'mock returned wrong shape' OR 'test passed but production failed' in TypeScript/Jest repos
patterns.aiNativeReason: AI generates both the code and the test in the same session with the same context. The mock reflects what the AI assumed the dependency returns — if that assumption is wrong, the test is a circular proof of nothing

patterns.name: AI Test Suite Has No Boundary or Edge Case Assertions
patterns.description: AI generates a test suite with high line coverage but only tests happy-path inputs — the exact values used in examples. Empty arrays, zero, null, empty string, max integer, duplicate keys: none appear. Optinum probes these boundaries by design because they are the inputs real users send and LLMs never generate tests for.

testPattern.description: Probe boundary values: empty, null, zero, max, duplicate

patterns.ossEvidence: Reference: 'Why AI-Generated Tests Are Not Enough' — documented pattern across Copilot/ChatGPT test generation studies showing 90%+ happy-path bias in AI-written test suites. OSS-search: repos where AI generated tests but coverage drops to 0% on error paths.
patterns.aiNativeReason: Training data contains far more success-path examples than failure-path examples. AI reproduces the distribution it was trained on — tests cover what the training data showed being tested

patterns.name: Error Path Exists in Code but Has No Test
patterns.description: AI writes a function with explicit error handling (try/catch, error return, 400/500 status branch) but writes no test for the error case. The error path is syntactically correct but functionally unverified — it may swallow errors, return wrong shape, or crash on a different input. Optinum generates a test that deliberately triggers the error path.

testPattern.description: Trigger error path and verify error response shape and status code

patterns.ossEvidence: OSS-search: PRs titled 'fix error handling' OR 'add error case test' across Node.js/Python API repos — these are post-hoc fixes for exactly this pattern after production failures
patterns.aiNativeReason: AI writes error handling because it has seen the pattern. It does not write the test for it because the training data for test generation overwhelmingly shows success path tests. The error branch exists but is never exercised
